mediaWork.title: Perspectives and Emotions
mediaWork.creatorName: Marcellus "Khaliifah" Williams (also known as Khaliifah ibn Rayford Daniels 'Abdul-Qudduus)
mediaWork.publisherOrNetwork: MADPmo.org (Missourians for Alternatives to the Death Penalty)
mediaWork.focusOrTheme: A collection of poetry exploring the perspectives and emotions of a man wrongfully convicted and sentenced to death row
mediaWork.summaryNotes: "Perspectives and Emotions" is unique among books about wrongful convictions as it is a collection of poetry written by a person who maintained his innocence until his execution, rather than a legal or journalistic account of wrongful conviction cases. The poetry provides a deeply personal and emotional perspective on the experience of being wrongfully convicted and facing execution. The book was published just weeks before Williams' execution, making it one of his final artistic expressions.  Williams' poetry explores themes of isolation, hope, spirituality, and human connection from the perspective of someone facing execution while maintaining his innocence. His work as an imam and mentor to other prisoners is also reflected in his writing, showing how he found purpose and meaning despite his circumstances. This book offers a rare first-person creative perspective on wrongful conviction.
